Protein in glycerol and water

A protein solvated by a mixture of glycerol and water, 50% in mass, in a periodic box: a system of the ComplexMixtures.jl examples, where the solvation of the protein by each component of the mixture is studied. The protein is fixed at the center of the box, and the mixture fills the rest of it.

The protein, glycerol (green) and water, in the half of the box behind the protein, with the edges of the periodic box (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom).

Files: protein.pdb, glycerol.pdb, water.pdb, and the input file protein_glycerol.inp.

The numbers of molecules

The box is a cube with sides of 76 Å, which leaves at least 12 Å of solvent around the protein (its largest dimension is 51 Å). The mixture of glycerol (92.09 g/mol) and water (18.02 g/mol), 50% in mass, has a density of 1.126 g/mL. In 1 g of it there are 0.5/92.09 mol of glycerol and 0.5/18.02 mol of water, so its number densities are:

  • glycerol: 1.126 × (0.5/92.09) × 0.6022 = 0.00368 molecules per Å³;
  • water: 1.126 × (0.5/18.02) × 0.6022 = 0.01882 molecules per Å³.

The protein (27.3 kDa) occupies about 27300/(1.35 × 0.6022) = 33600 Å³ (the density of proteins is about 1.35 g/mL), so the solution has 76³ − 33600 = 405400 Å³: 1493 molecules of glycerol and 7630 of water.

Tip

The SolutionBoxUSC recipe (see Recipes) computes these numbers from the density of the mixture as a function of its concentration, given as a table, in any concentration unit.

The protein at the center of the box

#
# A protein in a mixture of glycerol and water, 50% in mass (1.126 g/mL),
# in a periodic cubic box with sides of 76 Å.
#
tolerance 2.0
output protein_glycerol.pdb
pbc -38. -38. -38. 38. 38. 38.

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# The protein, fixed with its center at the center of the box
structure protein.pdb
  number 1
  center
  fixed 0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.
end structure

structure glycerol.pdb
  number 1493
end structure

structure water.pdb
  number 7630
end structure

The periodic box confines the molecules of the solvent, so they need no constraint. The protein is fixed with its geometric center (center) at the center of the box: all its atoms must be inside the periodic box (see Fixed molecules).

Check the initial placement first

Uncomment the check_initial_placement line of the input file, and run it as below (see Checking the initial placement): the initial placement, written to the output file (protein_glycerol.pdb) in a fraction of a second, shows the protein at the center of the box, and the solvent around it. Then comment the line again, and run the packing.

Packing

packmol protein_glycerol.inp

The packing (about 48 thousand atoms) takes about half a second.

Julia script

using Packmolprotein = structure_type("protein.pdb";    number = 1,    fixed = ([0., 0., 0.], [0., 0., 0.]),    center = :geometric,)glycerol = structure_type("glycerol.pdb"; number = 1493)water = structure_type("water.pdb"; number = 7630)system = PackmolSystem([protein, glycerol, water];    output = "protein_glycerol.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [76. 0. 0.; 0. 76. 0.; 0. 0. 76.], # centered at the origin    # check_initial_placement = true, # uncomment to only place the molecules)packmol(system)

As with the input file, check the initial placement first, with check_initial_placement = true (commented in the code above).

Settings

This document was generated with Documenter.jl version 1.19.0 on Thursday 19 November 2026. Using Julia version 1.13.4.

PackmolSystem(structure_types::Vector{<:StructureType}; output::String, kwargs...)

Build a PackmolSystem directly from a vector of StructureTypes (see structure_type), without going through an input file.

packmol(input_file::String; options...) packmol(packmol_system::PackmolSystem; options...) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., ) packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., ) packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Read a Packmol input file, run the packing optimization, and write the output.

structure_type(filename; number, constraints=Constraint[], tolerance=2.0, radius=nothing, fixed=nothing, center=:none, residue_numbering=-1, D=3, T=Float64)

Build a StructureType for number copies of the molecule read from the PDB file filename, without going through an input file.

packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Builds and packs a membrane protein system, without writing an input file (as write_packmol_input followed by packmol).

packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a lipid membrane system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent + Cossolvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, # or :orthorhombic, :dodecahedral, :octahedral kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Water + Ions system, without writing an input file.
